acceptance_criteria: A reference design (authored independently from public_spec.interface only) and the submission produce bit-identical rdata0/rdata1 waveforms cycle-by-cycle under randomized write/read/collision/reset sequences for at least 500 simulated clock cycles across multiple random seeds.
The submission compiles cleanly with iverilog against the generated testbench with zero errors and zero unresolved references.
The empty/naive baseline submission (a stub module that ties rdata0/rdata1 to constant 0 or passes through raw inputs) must fail the cycle-accurate comparison.
No submission that adds a one-cycle read latency, a combinational-bypass-only collision fix that glitches, or an asynchronous reset passes the behavioral simulation.
ground_truth: The gate-level netlist and obfuscated wrapper implement a 4x8 register file: an internal reg [7:0] mem[0:3] array updated synchronously (synchronous active-high reset clears all entries to 0, else on we=1 mem[waddr] <= wdata), with two fully combinational read ports assign rdata0 = mem[raddr0]; assign rdata1 = mem[raddr1]; so that same-address reads observe the newly written value starting the cycle after the write edge (standard synchronous-write, combinational-read register file with natural write-forwarding via the registered array read after the clock edge, i.e. no explicit bypass mux is needed or should be added).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Testbench toggles raddr0/raddr1 mid-cycle (without a clock edge) after a write has committed and checks that rdata updates within the same simulation time step, with no dependency on an additional posedge clk.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered design must not introduce any extra pipeline latency on the read ports (they must remain purely combinational with zero cycles from address change to data observation), since a hidden extra register stage would desynchronize any downstream logic depending on immediate read-after-write visibility.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Testbench applies back-to-back same-address write-then-read collisions across many random seeds and checks the read value transitions cleanly to the new data with no intermediate glitch value observed via zero-delay sampling immediately after the clock edge.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered design must not implement the write-forwarding/collision case using a combinational bypass multiplexer that could race with the clocked update and produce nondeterministic or glitchy output; the correct fix is that the read simply observes the already-updated synchronous register on the next delta cycle after the edge.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Testbench writes distinct nonzero patterns to all 4 addresses, asserts rst for one cycle, then immediately samples all reads (without any intervening write) and requires 0x00 on every address for both read ports.
security_requirements.requirement: Reset must clear all four entries synchronously and must not leave stale data observable on any read port even transiently after reset is asserted and before the first post-reset write, avoiding disclosure of previously stored bytes.

threat_model: An undocumented register-file block cannot be safely reused or replaced in a larger design when its exact port timing (write latency, reset semantics, and read/write collision policy) is concealed by gate-level flattening. A reverse engineer who infers the wrong collision policy (e.g. assuming the read returns the OLD value on a same-cycle collision, or adding an unnecessary one-cycle read latency) will produce a drop-in replacement that silently corrupts data paths relying on immediate write-visibility, and could also introduce inconsistent reads (e.g. combinational races) that leak stale bytes to a read port under adversarial address toggling.
